Gives the Jacobi catalytic carbon tank and the 10% crosslinked resin tank their own dedicated high-capacity vessels. Each media bed works at full strength, ideal for larger households and heavy water use.

No salt bags, no brine discharge, no regeneration cycles. Keeps healthy minerals in your water while stopping them from sticking to pipes and appliances.

## Water problems and how they are treated

### Hard Water
Cause: Minnesota groundwater is naturally hard. Dissolved calcium and magnesium picked up from limestone and dolomite bedrock stay in the water all the way to your tap.
Treatment: 10% crosslinked resin trades the calcium and magnesium for sodium ions before water reaches your plumbing. For homes that want scale protection without salt, a salt-free conditioner reduces scale adhesion but does not remove the minerals.

### White Scale
Cause: When hard water evaporates or is heated, dissolved calcium carbonate comes out of solution and hardens into chalky white scale on faucets, showerheads, glass and inside water heaters.
Treatment: Softening removes the hardness minerals so there is nothing left to deposit. Existing scale stops growing and is far easier to clean.

### Spots on Dishes
Cause: Mineral residue left behind when hard water dries on glassware and dishes. Detergent also works less effectively in hard water, so film builds up.
Treatment: Softened water dries clean. Most homeowners notice the difference on glassware within the first few loads.

### Dry Skin / Hair
Cause: Hardness minerals react with soap to form a film that is hard to rinse away, leaving skin and hair feeling dry and dull. Chlorine in city water adds to the effect.
Treatment: Softening removes the minerals that cause soap film. On city water, the Jacobi catalytic carbon tank also removes chlorine and chloramine before the shower.

### Chlorine Taste / Odor
Cause: Municipal utilities add chlorine or chloramine to keep water safe on its way through the distribution system. It does its job in the pipes, but the taste and smell arrive at your tap along with it.
Treatment: The Jacobi catalytic carbon tank is selected specifically because it treats chloramine as well as free chlorine. Every whole-home city system includes it, so showers, laundry and every faucet get treated water.

### Iron Staining
Cause: Dissolved iron is common in Minnesota well water. It is invisible coming out of the well, then oxidizes on contact with air and leaves orange-brown stains on sinks, tubs, toilets and laundry.
Treatment: Air-oxidation (AIO) treatment converts dissolved iron into solid particles inside the tank, and Katalox Light media captures them. Heavier iron loads get hydrogen peroxide injection ahead of filtration. A softener alone is not the right tool for real iron.

### Metallic Taste
Cause: Usually dissolved iron or manganese. Both are common in Minnesota groundwater and both leave a distinct metallic taste long before they stain.
Treatment: The same oxidation-plus-filtration process that stops staining removes the taste. Reverse osmosis at the kitchen sink polishes drinking water further.

### Rotten-Egg / Sulfur Odor
Cause: Hydrogen sulfide gas, produced by naturally occurring bacteria in groundwater or in a water heater. You smell it most at hot taps and first thing in the morning.
Treatment: Hydrogen sulfide needs chemical oxidation. Our Iron & Sulfur Treatment System injects hydrogen peroxide ahead of the Jacobi catalytic carbon tank, then softens. It is the one system we install for rotten-egg odor.

### Manganese
Cause: Manganese occurs naturally in Minnesota groundwater. It causes black or dark-brown staining and an unpleasant taste, and the Minnesota Department of Health publishes guidance on manganese levels in drinking water.
Treatment: Manganese is treated alongside iron: air oxidation converts it to a solid and Katalox Light media captures it. Your well test tells us the level and the right configuration. Reverse osmosis adds a second barrier for drinking water.

### Sediment
Cause: Sand, silt and rust particles drawn in by the well pump or shed by aging pipes. It clogs aerators and wears out downstream equipment.
Treatment: A pre-system sediment filter captures debris before it reaches your softener, media and valves. Recommended on most well installs.

### Drinking-Water Concerns
Cause: Whole-home treatment fixes hardness and taste, but the water you drink deserves a finer barrier. Dissolved solids, residual taste and the cost and clutter of bottled water are the usual reasons homeowners add reverse osmosis.
Treatment: A dedicated under-sink RO system pushes water through a semipermeable membrane and delivers it to its own faucet. Choose a compact tankless unit with remineralization or the proven tank configuration. A tank RO is included free with any whole-home system; the tankless is a $200 upgrade.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do you come to my home for a consultation?
Consultations are phone calls: you call or text us, we set a time and call you, go over your water and your home, recommend the right system at its published price and set your installation date. In-home presentations are available on request. Either way, the only required visit is the installation itself.

### How much does a whole-home system cost?
Every price is published on our pricing page. Whole-home city systems run $2,999 to $4,499 and well systems $4,499 to $5,999, with a reverse osmosis drinking-water system included free. Reverse osmosis on its own is $799 for the tank system or $999 for the tankless HW800 AlkaPro, a pre-sediment filter is $399 and a UV purifier is $899. Financing options are available, and travel fees may apply beyond 35 miles from Minneapolis.

### What is the difference between filtration and softening?
A water softener uses ion exchange to remove calcium and magnesium hardness. Carbon filtration targets different problems, mainly chlorine and chloramine taste and odor. They solve different things, which is why our whole-home city systems combine both.

### Do I need a different system for well water?
Usually, yes. City-water treatment focuses on hardness and municipal disinfectants. Private wells often also carry iron, sulfur, manganese and sediment, which need oxidation and filtration that a softener alone cannot handle. We keep the two system lines separate so you never pay for equipment your water does not need.

### What does reverse osmosis do?
Reverse osmosis pushes water through a semipermeable membrane that rejects a broad range of dissolved solids, then delivers the treated water to a dedicated faucet at your kitchen sink. It is a point-of-use system for drinking and cooking water, not a whole-home system, which is why we pair it with whole-home treatment.

### Tank RO or tankless RO — what's the difference?
A tank system slowly fills a pressurized storage tank so purified water is ready instantly. A tankless system treats water on demand, takes up far less under-sink space and has no storage tank. The tank system is $799 and the tankless HW800 AlkaPro is $999 on their own. With any whole-home system, the tank RO is included free and the tankless is a $200 upgrade.

### Can the reverse osmosis system be installed in the basement?
Yes. The standard installation puts the RO unit under the kitchen sink with its own drinking-water faucet. If you'd prefer the unit in the basement, basement RO installation is an additional $500. You can add it on any system page or just mention it on the call.

### Does the system treat every faucet?
Whole-home systems are installed where water enters the house, so every shower, faucet and appliance receives treated water. Reverse osmosis is the exception: it treats drinking water at one dedicated faucet.

### Is salt-free conditioning the same as a softener?
No. Salt-free conditioning reduces how much scale sticks to surfaces but leaves calcium and magnesium in the water. You will not get the slick soft-water feel of an ion-exchange softener. It is the right choice for homeowners who specifically want to avoid salt.

### How much maintenance is required?
Whole-home systems backwash and regenerate themselves automatically. Your part is keeping the brine tank topped up with salt on softening systems and swapping reverse osmosis filters on schedule, which twist out by hand on the tankless unit. Well add-ons like the sediment filter and UV lamp are replaced periodically.

### How often do I add salt?
It depends on your water hardness and how much water your household uses. We size the system and set the regeneration schedule for your home at installation and show you how to check the brine tank.

### Will installation affect my water pressure?
Systems are sized for real households. Our whole-home city system is rated for 28 GPM system flow and the dual-tank well system for 27 GPM, so showers, laundry and sprinklers can run together.

### How long does installation take?
Most installations are completed in a single visit. We connect the equipment to your main water line, configure it for your water and walk you through how it works before we leave.

### Should my well water be tested?
Yes, especially if you suspect iron, sulfur or manganese. Treatment depends on the form and concentration of the problem, so we go over testing on the call and set the final configuration from the results.

### What warranty is included?
Whole-home and reverse osmosis systems carry a lifetime warranty on the system. We go through the exact terms with you on the phone before anything is installed.

### How do I schedule?
Call or text (952) 952-6206 any time. We answer within 24 hours, set a time for your free phone consultation, and you get a confirmation right away. No deposit is required.

### How does the Best Price Guarantee work?
Bring us a competing written quote on comparable equipment and installation and we will beat the price. Best-price customers also get priority booking on the schedule.
